name: hook
text: Can π really equal four? Let's find out.

name: setup
text: Start with a circle of diameter one, wrapped in a square. The square's perimeter is four.

name: fold
text: Now fold the corners inward, step by step. Each stage is a staircase of horizontal and vertical steps. Its perimeter stays at four.

name: converge
text: The staircase hugs the circle more and more tightly. Every point gets arbitrarily close to it.

name: paradox
text: So shouldn't the circle's length be four too? But π is about 3.14. Something is wrong.

name: taxi_sibling
text: Picture a taxi on a city grid. It must drive along the streets. A bird flies straight across. Here, the taxi drives two units, while the bird's straight line is about 1.41.

name: taxi_circle
text: Now measure the circle the taxi way: add up every horizontal and vertical move. Around this circle, the taxi distance is exactly four.

name: resolution
text: The true length is π. So four is not the circle's length. It is the length of the wrong ruler.

name: lesson
text: The lesson: shapes can converge while their lengths don't. Always check the direction, not just the position.
